title.zh: 卷430 列傳二百十七 雷正绾 陶茂林 曹克忠 胡中和 何胜必 萧庆高 杨復东 周达武 李辉武 唐友耕
title.en: Volume 430 Biographies 217: Lei Zhengwan, Tao Maolin, Cao Kezhong, Hu Zhonghe, He Shengbi, Xiao Qinggao, Yang Fudong, Zhou Dawu, Li Huiwu, Tang Yougeng
title.raw: 卷430 列傳二百十七 雷正绾 陶茂林 曹克忠 胡中和 何胜必 萧庆高 杨復东 周达武 李辉武 唐友耕

sentences.zh: 列傳二百十七

translations.literal: Biographies 217
translations.idiomatic: Biography 217

sentences.zh: 雷正綰陶茂林曹克忠胡中和何勝必蕭慶高楊復東

translations.literal: Lei Zhengwan, Tao Maolin, Cao Kezhong, Hu Zhonghe, He Shengbi, Xiao Qinggao, Yang Fudong
translations.idiomatic: Lei Zhengwan, Tao Maolin, Cao Kezhong, Hu Zhonghe, He Shengbi, Xiao Qinggao, and Yang Fudong

sentences.zh: 周達武李輝武唐友耕

translations.literal: Zhou Dawu, Li Huiwu, Tang Yougeng
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dawu, Li Huiwu, and Tang Yougeng

sentences.zh: 雷正綰，字偉堂，四川中江人。

translations.literal: Lei Zhengwan, style name Weitang, was a native of Zhongjiang in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Zhengwan, whose courtesy name was Weitang, came from Zhongjiang in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 由把總從軍湖北，積功至游擊，賜號直勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Starting as a platoon commander, he joined the army in Hubei, accumulated merit until he reached brigade commander, and was granted the title Zhiyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service in Hubei as a platoon commander, rose through merit to brigade commander, and was awarded the title Zhiyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 咸豐八年，從多隆阿援安徽石牌、潛山、太湖、桐城，諸戰皆功最，累擢副將，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xianfeng, he followed Duolong'a to relieve Anhui at Shipai, Qianshan, Taihu, and Tongcheng; in every battle his merit ranked first, and he was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander and recorded by name for major general.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Xianfeng reign (1858), he followed Duolong'a to Anhui, fighting at Shipai, Qianshan, Taihu, and Tongcheng; in each engagement his merit ranked first, and he was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander and placed on the register for major general.

sentences.zh: 十一年，敗黃文金於蔣家山、項家河、江家河、麻子嶺，一月五捷，授陝安鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he defeated Huang Wenjin at Jiangjiashan, Xiangjiahe, Jiangjiahe, and Maziling; within one month he won five victories and was appointed major general of Shaan'an Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1861), he defeated Huang Wenjin at Jiangjiashan, Xiangjiahe, Jiangjiahe, and Maziling, winning five victories in a single month, and was appointed major general of the Shaan'an garrison.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，克廬州，以提督記名。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he captured Luzhou and was recorded by name for provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign (1862), he captured Luzhou and was placed on the register for provincial commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 從多隆阿援陝西，詔正綰先赴本任，未至，擢陝西提督，幫辦軍務，駐西安。

translations.literal: He followed Duolong'a to relieve Shaanxi; an edict ordered Zhengwan to proceed first to his original post, but before he arrived he was promoted to Shaanxi provincial commander-in-chief, assigned to assist in military affairs, and stationed at Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Duolong'a to Shaanxi; the court ordered Zhengwan to take up his post first, but before he arrived he was promoted to provincial commander-in-chief of Shaanxi, assigned to assist in military affairs, and stationed at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 二年，多隆阿既克東路，令正綰規三原，屢破賊。

translations.literal: In the second year, after Duolong'a had pacified the eastern route, he ordered Zhengwan to target Sanyuan and repeatedly defeated the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1863), after Duolong'a had secured the eastern front, he ordered Zhengwan to advance on Sanyuan and repeatedly routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 會解鳳翔圍，進援甘肅，連戰靈臺、鎮原，皆捷。

translations.literal: He then helped lift the siege of Fengxiang, advanced to relieve Gansu, and fought successive battles at Lingtai and Zhenyuan, all victorious.
translations.idiomatic: He then helped raise the siege of Fengxiang, advanced into Gansu, and won successive victories at Lingtai and Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 三年，破賊崇仁、新城，進逼平原。

translations.literal: In the third year, he defeated the rebels at Chongren and Xincheng and pressed toward Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1864), he defeated the rebels at Chongren and Xincheng and pressed toward Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 會多隆阿卒於軍，都興阿繼督師甘肅，正綰仍奉命為副。

translations.literal: When Duolong'a died in camp, Duxing'a succeeded as commander of Gansu forces, and Zhengwan remained ordered to serve as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Duolong'a died in camp, Duxing'a took command in Gansu, and Zhengwan continued to serve as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 克平涼，斬賊首鐵酉、羽輕林，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: He captured Pingliang and beheaded the rebel leaders Tie You and Yu Qinglin, and was granted a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Pingliang and beheaded the rebel leaders Tie You and Yu Qinglin, and was awarded a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 於是固原踞賊悉竄龍山鎮，追擊敗之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the rebels holding Guyuan all fled to Longshan Town, and he pursued and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels holding Guyuan then fled to Longshan Town, and he pursued and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 賊回竄，又陷固原。

translations.literal: The rebels doubled back and again seized Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels doubled back and seized Guyuan again.

sentences.zh: 正綰疾趨蓮花城，欲襲其巢穴，遇伏，受矛傷，部下亡千餘人，裹創攻蓮花城，克之，詔嘉其勇。

translations.literal: Zhengwan hastened to Lianhuacheng intending to strike their nest, met an ambush, and was wounded by a spear; more than a thousand of his men perished. Binding his wounds, he attacked Lianhuacheng, captured it, and an edict praised his valor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengwan rushed to Lianhuacheng to strike their stronghold, walked into an ambush, and was speared; more than a thousand of his men fell. He bound his wounds, pressed the attack, and took the town; the court praised his courage.

sentences.zh: 四年春，克固原，進攻黑城子，斬賊首黑虎。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, he recovered Guyuan, advanced against Heichengzi, and beheaded the rebel leader Heihu.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year (1865), he recovered Guyuan, advanced on Heichengzi, and beheaded the rebel leader Heihu.

sentences.zh: 克官橋、李旺二堡，擒賊首木棍等。

translations.literal: He captured the two forts of Guanqiao and Liwang and seized the rebel leaders Mugun and others.
translations.idiomatic: He took the forts at Guanqiao and Liwang and captured the rebel leaders Mugun and others.

sentences.zh: 乘勝薄預望城，破下馬關、半​​角城賊壘，進規靈州，分兵解安定圍。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory, he approached Yuwangcheng, broke the rebel stockades at Xiamaguan and Banjiaocheng, advanced to target Lingzhou, and detached troops to lift the siege of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Riding the momentum, he pressed toward Yuwangcheng, stormed the rebel camps at Xiamaguan and Banjiaocheng, advanced on Lingzhou, and detached a force to raise the siege of Anding.

sentences.zh: 七月，偕曹克忠攻金積堡，軍餉不繼，為賊所圍，飢潰。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, together with Cao Kezhong he attacked Jinjibao; army supplies failed, they were surrounded by rebels, and the troops broke in hunger.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, he joined Cao Kezhong in an assault on Jinjibao; supplies ran out, the rebels surrounded them, and the army collapsed from hunger.

sentences.zh: 正綰自劾，褫勇號、黃馬褂，黜幫辦，歸總督楊岳斌節制。

translations.literal: Zhengwan memorialized against himself; his Batulu title and yellow jacket were stripped, his post assisting military affairs was removed, and he was placed under the command of Governor-General Yang Yuebin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengwan submitted a self-accusation; his Batulu title and yellow jacket were stripped, he was removed from his assisting post, and placed under Governor-General Yang Yuebin.

sentences.zh: 正綰弟總兵雷恆及副將李高啟等以主將失職，煽亂，犯涇州，正綰不能制止，憤欲自裁。

translations.literal: Zhengwan's younger brother, Major General Lei Heng, and Deputy Commander Li Gaoqi and others, citing the commander's dereliction, incited mutiny and attacked Jingzhou; Zhengwan could not stop them and in anger wished to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengwan's brother, Major General Lei Heng, and Deputy Commander Li Gaoqi and others, blaming the commander's failure, incited a mutiny and marched on Jingzhou; Zhengwan could not restrain them and in despair sought to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 詔念前功，不加罪，責令整軍勦賊圖自贖。

translations.literal: An edict, mindful of his former merit, imposed no punishment and ordered him to reorganize his army, suppress the rebels, and seek redemption.
translations.idiomatic: The court, mindful of his past service, imposed no punishment and ordered him to reorganize his troops, suppress the rebels, and redeem himself.

sentences.zh: 命巡撫趙長齡會楊岳斌按訊，正綰縛送雷恆等置之法。

translations.literal: The court ordered Governor Zhao Changling to join Yang Yuebin in investigating; Zhengwan bound and sent Lei Heng and the others to be punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Governor Zhao Changling to investigate jointly with Yang Yuebin; Zhengwan bound Lei Heng and the others and handed them over for punishment.

sentences.zh: 當事變初起，謠諑紛淆，詔斥劉蓉張皇妄奏，許正綰專摺奏事以慰之。

translations.literal: When the incident first broke out, rumors and slander were confused; an edict rebuked Liu Rong for alarmist false reports and permitted Zhengwan to submit memorials on his own authority to reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis first erupted, rumors flew in every direction; the court rebuked Liu Rong for alarmist false reports and allowed Zhengwan to file memorials directly, by way of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 所部招集增募僅三千人。

translations.literal: His command, through recruitment and enlargement, amounted to only three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Through recruitment and re-enlistment, his command numbered only three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 五年，蘭州兵變，回匪窺伺，正綰支拄於平涼、固原之間，破賊於橫河川，克平涼，复黃馬褂、勇號。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, when the Lanzhou garrison mutinied and Muslim rebels watched for openings, Zhengwan held the line between Pingliang and Guyuan, defeated rebels at Henghechuan, recovered Pingliang, and regained his yellow jacket and Batulu title.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1866), when the Lanzhou garrison mutinied and Muslim rebels pressed their advantage, Zhengwan held the line between Pingliang and Guyuan, routed the rebels at Henghechuan, retook Pingliang, and recovered his yellow jacket and Batulu title.

sentences.zh: 六年，左宗​​棠入陝督師，正綰率軍助剿，援慶陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Zuo Zongtang entered Shaanxi to command the army; Zhengwan led troops to assist in suppression and relieved Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1867), Zuo Zongtang took command in Shaanxi; Zhengwan led his army to assist and relieved Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 七年，兩破賊於長武，克黃家堡。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he twice defeated rebels at Changwu and captured Huangjiabao.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1868), he twice defeated the rebels at Changwu and captured Huangjiabao.

sentences.zh: 八年，會攻董志原，克之，晉號達春巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he joined the assault on Dongzhiyuan, captured it, and was advanced to the title Dachun Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1869), he joined the assault on Dongzhiyuan, took it, and was promoted to the title Dachun Batulu.

sentences.zh: 又破白彥虎於李旺堡。

translations.literal: He again defeated Bai Yanhu at Liwangbao.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated Bai Yanhu at Liwangbao.

sentences.zh: 會攻金積堡，當西路，屢克要隘，合圍。

translations.literal: He joined the assault on Jinjibao, holding the western route, repeatedly capturing strategic passes and completing the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the siege of Jinjibao on the western front, repeatedly took key passes, and helped complete the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 及馬化隆伏誅，被優敘。

translations.literal: When Ma Hualong was executed, he received preferential commendation.
translations.idiomatic: After Ma Hualong was executed, he received special commendation for his service.

sentences.zh: 光緒十年，法越兵事起，命率甘軍駐鳳凰城，固邊防，事定回任。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Guangxu, when the Franco-Vietnamese war broke out, he was ordered to lead Gansu troops to garrison Fenghuangcheng to secure the frontier; when affairs were settled he returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Guangxu reign (1884), when war broke out between France and Vietnam, he was ordered to lead Gansu troops to Fenghuangcheng to hold the frontier; when the crisis passed he returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 兩遇萬壽慶典，加太子少保、尚書銜。

translations.literal: On two occasions of longevity celebrations he was given the additional titles Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On two imperial birthday celebrations he was granted the additional titles Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，循化撒回倡亂，督剿無功，革職留任。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, when the Salar Muslims of Xunhua rose in rebellion, he supervised suppression without success and was dismissed from office but retained on duty.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year (1895), when the Salar Muslims of Xunhua rebelled, he directed suppression without success and was stripped of rank but kept at his post.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，罷，卒於家，仍以前勞賜卹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was dismissed, died at home, and posthumous honors were still granted for his former labors.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year (1897) he was dismissed, died at home, and posthumous honors were granted in recognition of his earlier service.

sentences.zh: 陶茂林，湖南長沙人。

translations.literal: Tao Maolin was a native of Changsha in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Maolin came from Changsha in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 以武童入湘軍，轉戰湖北、江西，積功至游擊。

translations.literal: Entering the Xiang Army as a military student, he fought in Hubei and Jiangxi and accumulated merit until brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Xiang Army as a military cadet, campaigned in Hubei and Jiangxi, and rose through merit to brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 咸豐八年，胡林翼調為楚軍營官，扼黃州，破賊霍山、舒城，克建德，擢參將。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xianfeng, Hu Lin'yi transferred him as camp officer of the Chu Army to hold Huangzhou; he defeated rebels at Huoshan and Shucheng, captured Jiande, and was promoted to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Xianfeng reign (1858), Hu Lin'yi assigned him as a Chu Army camp officer to hold Huangzhou; he routed rebels at Huoshan and Shucheng, took Jiande, and was promoted to colonel.

sentences.zh: 十年，從多隆阿破賊於桐城掛車河，擢副將。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, following Duolong'a he defeated rebels at Guachehe in Tongcheng and was promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1860), he followed Duolong'a and defeated rebels at Guachehe near Tongcheng, and was promoted to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 十一年，破賊施家山，擒其渠，及克安慶，賜號鍾勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he defeated rebels at Shijiashan and captured their leader; when Anqing was taken he was granted the title Zhongyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1861), he defeated rebels at Shijiashan and captured their leader; when Anqing fell he was awarded the title Zhongyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，克廬州，先登，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he captured Luzhou, was first to scale the walls, and was recorded by name for major general.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign (1862), he captured Luzhou, was first over the wall, and was placed on the register for major general.

sentences.zh: 遂從多隆阿西征，破賊於武關。

translations.literal: He then followed Duolong'a on the western campaign and defeated rebels at Wuguan.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Duolong'a west and defeated the rebels at Wuguan.

sentences.zh: 從剿回匪，解同州圍。

translations.literal: He joined in suppressing the Muslim rebels and lifted the siege of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against the Muslim rebels and raised the siege of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 克羌白鎮、王閣村賊巢，功皆最，授漢中鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He captured the rebel nests at Qiangbaizhen and Wanggecun; his merit ranked first in each case, and he was appointed major general of Hanzhong Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He took the rebel strongholds at Qiangbaizhen and Wanggecun, ranking first in merit each time, and was appointed major general of the Hanzhong garrison.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔被圍久，茂林率三千人往援，連戰解圍，擢甘肅提督。

translations.literal: Fengxiang had been besieged for a long time; Maolin led three thousand men to relieve it, won successive battles to lift the siege, and was promoted to Gansu provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang had been under siege for a long time; Maolin led three thousand men to its relief, fought his way through in successive battles, and was promoted to provincial commander-in-chief of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 粵匪出寶雞山口，擾郿縣、盩厔，茂林要擊雨門鎮、二嶺關，迭敗之。

translations.literal: Cantonese rebels emerged from Baoji Pass and harassed Mei County and Zhouzhi; Maolin intercepted them at Yumen Town and Erying Pass and repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping forces came out through Baoji Pass and raided Mei County and Zhouzhi; Maolin intercepted them at Yumen Town and Erying Pass and defeated them repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 進克汧陽、隴州。

translations.literal: He advanced and captured Qianyang and Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and captured Qianyang and Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 遂會雷正綰分道規平涼，陣斬賊首木仲沅訥三等，克之，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: He then joined Lei Zhengwan in separate columns to target Pingliang, slew in battle the rebel leaders Muzhongyuenne and others of the third rank, captured it, and was granted a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Lei Zhengwan in a pincer on Pingliang, killed the rebel leaders Muzhongyuenne and others in battle, took the city, and was awarded a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 進拔張家川賊巢，破龍山鎮、蓮花城援賊，解安定圍。

translations.literal: He advanced to seize the rebel nest at Zhangjiachuan, defeated relief forces from Longshan Town and Lianhuacheng, and lifted the siege of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on the rebel stronghold at Zhangjiachuan, routed relief forces from Longshan Town and Lianhuacheng, and raised the siege of Anding.

sentences.zh: 克金縣，破賊惠城，擒其渠黑牙古。

translations.literal: He captured Jinxian, defeated rebels at Huicheng, and seized their leader Heiyagu.
translations.idiomatic: He took Jinxian, defeated the rebels at Huicheng, and captured their leader Heiyagu.

sentences.zh: 四年，克黑城賊巢，解靖遠圍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he captured the rebel nest at Heicheng and lifted the siege of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1865), he took the rebel stronghold at Heicheng and raised the siege of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 進攻會寧，所部索餉譁潰五營，賊乘之，六營皆陷。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Huining, five battalions of his command mutinied demanding pay; the rebels seized the opportunity and all six battalions were lost.
translations.idiomatic: As he advanced on Huining, five of his battalions mutinied over unpaid wages; the rebels pressed the advantage and all six battalions were overrun.

sentences.zh: 茂林調後路四營來援，突圍出，退駐安定。

translations.literal: Maolin called up four rear battalions to relieve him, broke out of encirclement, and withdrew to garrison Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Maolin brought up four rear battalions, fought his way out, and fell back to Anding.

sentences.zh: 巡撫劉蓉疏陳甘軍積弊，論茂林不職，茂林亦以兵潰自劾。

translations.literal: Governor Liu Rong memorialized on the chronic abuses of the Gansu army and judged Maolin derelict; Maolin also memorialized against himself for the troop collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Liu Rong reported on the chronic abuses of the Gansu army and judged Maolin unfit for command; Maolin submitted a self-accusation over the rout.

sentences.zh: 詔斥廢法營私，以致兵潰而叛，遂罷職，歸。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked him for abandoning discipline and seeking private gain, causing troops to break and rebel; he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The court rebuked him for corruption and lax discipline that had led to mutiny and rout; he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 十年，貴州巡撫曾璧光調茂林赴黔協剿。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Guizhou Governor Zeng Biguang transferred Maolin to Guizhou to assist in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1871), Guizhou Governor Zeng Biguang summoned Maolin to Guizhou to assist in suppression.

sentences.zh: 復新城，克安順賊巢，平古州、丹江苗，復原官。

translations.literal: He recovered Xincheng, captured the rebel nest at Anshun, pacified the Miao of Guzhou and Danjiang, and was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Xincheng, took the rebel stronghold at Anshun, pacified the Miao of Guzhou and Danjiang, and was restored to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，收復下江、永從各城，破六峒賊巢，加頭品頂戴，晉號愛星阿巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu, he recovered the cities of Xiajiang and Yongcong, destroyed the rebel nest at Liudong, was given the first-rank official's hat ornament, and was advanced to the title Aixing'a Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Guangxu reign (1876), he recovered the cities of Xiajiang and Yongcong, destroyed the rebel stronghold at Liudong, was granted the first-rank hat ornament, and was promoted to the title Aixing'a Batulu.

sentences.zh: 十六年，署古州鎮總兵，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he served as acting major general of Guzhou Garrison and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year (1890) he served as acting major general of the Guzhou garrison and died in office.

sentences.zh: 曹克忠，直隸天津人。

translations.literal: Cao Kezhong was a native of Tianjin in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Kezhong came from Tianjin in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 初投效湘軍，嗣從多隆阿，積功至都司。

translations.literal: At first he entered the Xiang Army, then followed Duolong'a, and accumulated merit until battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: He first joined the Xiang Army, then served under Duolong'a, and rose through merit to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，令募五百人為忠字營，大破援賊於潛山、太湖，洊擢參將，賜號悍勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng he was ordered to recruit five hundred men as the Zhongzi Battalion, greatly defeated relief rebels at Qianshan and Taihu, was repeatedly promoted to colonel, and granted the title Hanyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Xianfeng reign (1860), he was ordered to raise five hundred men as the Zhongzi Battalion, routed relief forces at Qianshan and Taihu, was repeatedly promoted to colonel, and was awarded the title Hanyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 掛車河之捷，擢副將。

translations.literal: For the victory at Guachehe he was promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: For the victory at Guachehe he was promoted to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 克桐城、宿松諸城，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: He captured Tongcheng, Susong, and other cities and was recorded by name for major general.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Tongcheng, Susong, and other cities and was placed on the register for major general.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，克廬州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he captured Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign (1862), he captured Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 後從多隆阿西征，武關、同州諸戰皆從。

translations.literal: Later he followed Duolong'a on the western campaign and took part in every battle at Wuguan, Tongzhou, and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Duolong'a west and fought in every engagement at Wuguan, Tongzhou, and beyond.

sentences.zh: 二年，攻羌白鎮，克忠單騎往諭賊，賊請降，察其詐，潛師會攻，下之，乘勝奪王閣村，予一品封典。

translations.literal: In the second year, attacking Qiangbaizhen, Kezhong went alone on horseback to persuade the rebels; they asked to surrender, but he detected deceit, secretly gathered forces for a joint assault, took the place, and pressing the victory seized Wanggecun; he was granted first-rank enfeoffment privileges.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1863), assaulting Qiangbaizhen, Kezhong rode out alone to parley with the rebels; they offered surrender, but he saw through the ruse, launched a coordinated surprise attack, took the town, and pressed on to seize Wanggecun; he was granted first-rank enfeoffment privileges.

sentences.zh: 尋率烏拉馬隊及楚勇七營屯長安、鄠縣之間。

translations.literal: Soon he led the Wula cavalry and seven battalions of Chu troops to encamp between Chang'an and Huxian.
translations.idiomatic: He soon led the Wula cavalry and seven Chu battalions to camp between Chang'an and Huxian.

sentences.zh: 光泰廟為入省要衝，賊踞之以扼糧路，克忠擊走之。

translations.literal: Guangtai Temple was a strategic pass into the province; rebels held it to choke the grain route, and Kezhong attacked and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Guangtai Temple guarded the main route into the province; rebels held it to cut the grain supply, and Kezhong drove them off.

sentences.zh: 分隊清西路餘匪，省城始安。

translations.literal: He detached columns to clear remaining bandits on the western route, and the provincial capital was finally secure.
translations.idiomatic: He detached columns to clear remaining rebels on the western front, and the provincial capital was finally secure.

sentences.zh: 以提督記名，授河州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He was recorded by name for provincial commander-in-chief and appointed major general of Hezhou Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was placed on the register for provincial commander-in-chief and appointed major general of the Hezhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 渡渭連破賊於白起營、馬家埠、白吉原，邠州平，陝回西趨。

translations.literal: Crossing the Wei, he repeatedly defeated rebels at Baiqiying, Majiabu, and Baijiyuan; Binzhou was pacified and the Shaanxi Muslims fled west.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Wei, he routed rebels at Baiqiying, Majiabu, and Baijiyuan in succession; Binzhou was pacified and the Shaanxi Muslim rebels fled west.

sentences.zh: 三年，平麟游諸匪。

translations.literal: In the third year, he pacified the bandits of Linyou and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1864), he pacified the rebels around Linyou.

sentences.zh: 會援甘肅，連破賊於西河口、黑水峪，赴河州本任。

translations.literal: He joined in relieving Gansu, repeatedly defeated rebels at Xihekou and Heishuiyu, and proceeded to his original post at Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the relief of Gansu, won successive victories at Xihekou and Heishuiyu, and took up his post at Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 克秦安，解秦州圍，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: He captured Qin'an, lifted the siege of Qinzhou, and was granted a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: He took Qin'an, raised the siege of Qinzhou, and was awarded a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 四年，攻蕭何城及馬定嘴，將台、隆德諸堡，悉平。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he attacked Xiaohecheng and Madingzui and the forts of Jiangtai, Longde, and others, pacifying them all.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1865), he attacked Xiaohecheng, Madingzui, and the forts at Jiangtai, Longde, and elsewhere, pacifying them all.

sentences.zh: 克海城，回匪並竄李旺堡、同心城，攻下之。

translations.literal: He captured Haicheng; Muslim rebels together fled to Liwangbao and Tongxincheng, and he attacked and took them.
translations.idiomatic: He took Haicheng; the Muslim rebels fled together to Liwangbao and Tongxincheng, and he stormed and captured both.

sentences.zh: 偕雷正綰規取金積堡，屯強家沙窩，數有斬獲。

translations.literal: Together with Lei Zhengwan he targeted Jinjibao, encamped at Qiangjiashawo, and repeatedly scored kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: With Lei Zhengwan he advanced on Jinjibao, encamped at Qiangjiashawo, and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 輕進，為賊所包鈔，正綰軍先潰，克忠亦退。

translations.literal: Advancing rashly, he was surrounded and cut off by rebels; Zhengwan's army broke first, and Kezhong also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced too boldly, was surrounded by the rebels, Zhengwan's force broke first, and Kezhong fell back as well.

sentences.zh: 因前功免罪，授甘肅提督。

translations.literal: Because of his former merit he was exempted from punishment and appointed Gansu provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: On account of his earlier service he was spared punishment and appointed provincial commander-in-chief of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 時陶茂林、雷正綰軍相繼譁變，回氛益熾，自楊岳斌楚軍外，僅克忠一軍與之相持。

translations.literal: At that time the armies of Tao Maolin and Lei Zhengwan mutinied in succession, Muslim rebel strength grew fiercer, and apart from Yang Yuebin's Chu Army only Kezhong's force held the line against them.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Maolin's and Lei Zhengwan's armies mutinied in turn, Muslim rebel power surged, and apart from Yang Yuebin's Chu forces only Kezhong's army still held the line.

sentences.zh: 克忠援鞏昌，賊敗走，又毀董家堡賊巢。

translations.literal: Kezhong relieved Gongchang; the rebels were defeated and fled, and he again destroyed the rebel nest at Dongjiabao.
translations.idiomatic: Kezhong relieved Gongchang, routed the rebels, and destroyed the rebel stronghold at Dongjiabao.

sentences.zh: 五年，援洮州，次李岐山，回目馬芳乞降，誅其酋丁重選等而還。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he relieved Taozhou, halted at Liqishan; the Muslim leader Ma Fang begged to surrender, and he executed the chiefs Ding Zhongxuan and others before returning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1866), he relieved Taozhou and halted at Liqishan; the Muslim leader Ma Fang sued for peace, and Kezhong executed the chiefs Ding Zhongxuan and others before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 蘭州標兵變，楊岳斌令克忠移軍鎮懾。

translations.literal: When the Lanzhou garrison troops mutinied, Yang Yuebin ordered Kezhong to move his army to overawe them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lanzhou garrison mutinied, Yang Yuebin ordered Kezhong to march in and restore order.

sentences.zh: 克忠至，人心稍定，然糧餉俱竭，乞病回籍。

translations.literal: When Kezhong arrived, morale steadied somewhat, but grain and pay were exhausted; he begged leave on grounds of illness and returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Kezhong's arrival steadied morale, but supplies and pay were exhausted; he requested sick leave and returned home.

sentences.zh: 十年，詔起赴陝接統淮軍，專防肅州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, an edict recalled him to Shaanxi to take command of the Huai Army and specialize in defending Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1871), the court recalled him to Shaanxi to take over the Huai Army and hold Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一年，所部有結會匪者，甘軍馬世俊騎兵亦變，降捻多叛應，克忠遣兵平之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, members of his command joined secret-society bandits; Gansu trooper Ma Shijun's cavalry also mutinied, and many surrendered Nian rebels rose in response; Kezhong sent troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1872), men in his command joined secret-society bandits; Ma Shijun's Gansu cavalry mutinied as well, and many surrendered Nian rebels rose in sympathy; Kezhong sent troops to put them down.

sentences.zh: 复乞病解軍事。

translations.literal: He again begged leave on grounds of illness and was relieved of military duties.
translations.idiomatic: He again requested sick leave and was relieved of military command.

sentences.zh: 十一年，署甘肅提督，尋解職歸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he served as acting Gansu provincial commander-in-chief, soon resigned, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he served as acting provincial commander-in-chief of Gansu, then resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 光緒九年，命募六營防山海關。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Guangxu, he was ordered to recruit six battalions to defend Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Guangxu reign (1883), he was ordered to raise six battalions to defend Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 十年，授廣東水師提督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was appointed naval commander-in-chief of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1884), he was appointed naval commander-in-chief of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 十一年，病罷，食全俸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was dismissed on grounds of illness and received his full salary.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1885) he was dismissed for illness and retained his full stipend.

sentences.zh: 二十年，命治天津團練，統津勝軍。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he was ordered to manage Tianjin militia training and command the Jinsheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year (1894), he was ordered to organize Tianjin militia and command the Jinsheng Army.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，卒，賜卹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he died and posthumous honors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year (1896) he died, and posthumous honors were granted.

sentences.zh: 胡中和，字元廷，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Hu Zhonghe, style name Yuanting, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhonghe, whose courtesy name was Yuanting, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，從湘軍剿粵匪，積功擢把總。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianfeng reign, he followed the Xiang Army in suppressing Cantonese rebels and through merit was promoted to platoon commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign, he served with the Xiang Army against the Taiping rebels and rose through merit to platoon commander.

sentences.zh: 六年，從蕭啟江援江西，复袁州，超擢都司，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, following Xiao Qijiang to relieve Jiangxi, he recovered Yuanzhou, was exceptionally promoted to battalion commander, and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1856), he followed Xiao Qijiang to Jiangxi, recovered Yuanzhou, was promoted ahead of schedule to battalion commander, and was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 七年，從克臨安，中砲傷，以游擊留湖南補用。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, following in the capture of Lin'an, he was struck by cannon fire; as brigade commander he was retained in Hunan for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1857), he took part in capturing Lin'an, was wounded by artillery, and was kept on in Hunan at the rank of brigade commander pending appointment.

sentences.zh: 八年，破賊上屯渡，乘勝复撫州，擢參將。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he defeated rebels at Shangtundu and, riding the victory, recovered Fuzhou; he was promoted to regimental commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1858), he routed the rebels at Shangtundu, pressed the advantage to retake Fuzhou, and was promoted to regimental commander.

sentences.zh: 九年，复南安，擢副將。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he recovered Nan'an and was promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1859), he retook Nan'an and was promoted to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 石達開由寶慶竄廣西，陷興安，遣黨攻桂林，自率悍賊屯大溶江。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai fled from Baqing into Guangxi, took Xing'an, sent partisans to attack Guilin, and himself led fierce rebels to encamp at the Darong River.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai broke out from Baqing into Guangxi, captured Xing'an, sent detachments against Guilin, and personally led elite rebel troops to camp on the Darong River.

sentences.zh: 中和從蕭啟江往援，大破賊於大溶江，賊竄貴州境，加總兵銜，賜號伊德克勒巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Zhonghe followed Xiao Qijiang to relieve them, thoroughly defeated the rebels at the Darong River; the rebels fled into Guizhou territory; he was given major-general rank and granted the title Yidekele Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe marched with Xiao Qijiang to the relief, crushed the rebels on the Darong River, and drove them into Guizhou; he received major-general rank and the title Yidekele Batulu.

sentences.zh: 十年，蕭啟江率軍援四川，中和從之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Xiao Qijiang led the army to relieve Sichuan, and Zhonghe followed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1860), Xiao Qijiang marched into Sichuan with his forces, and Zhonghe went with him.

sentences.zh: 啟江卒於軍，中和偕何勝必、蕭慶高等分領其眾。

translations.literal: Qijiang died in the army; Zhonghe together with He Shengbi and Xiao Qinggao and others divided command of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Qijiang died on campaign, Zhonghe, He Shengbi, Xiao Qinggao, and others jointly took over his command.

sentences.zh: 剿滇匪李永和於井研，連戰皆捷，賊解圍遁，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: He suppressed the Yunnan rebel Li Yonghe at Jingyan; every battle was victorious; the rebels lifted the siege and fled; he was recorded by name for major general.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against the Yunnan rebel Li Yonghe at Jingyan, won a string of victories, and forced the rebels to abandon their siege and flee; he was placed on the register for major general.

sentences.zh: 尋授四川建昌鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed major general of the Jianchang Garrison in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed major general of the Jianchang garrison in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 十一年，永和竄踞富順牛腹渡，兩岸築堅壘，背水而陣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Yonghe fled to occupy Niufudu in Fushun, building strong stockades on both banks and forming battle lines with their backs to the water.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1861), Yonghe seized Niufudu in Fushun, threw up fortified camps on both riverbanks, and drew up his lines with the water at his back.

sentences.zh: 中和選銳卒沿河設伏，自率羸師誘之，賊大出，伏發，截其歸路，俘斬無算，賊壘盡夷，進解大邑之圍，予二品封典。

translations.literal: Zhonghe selected crack troops to set ambushes along the river and himself led a weak force to lure them; the rebels came out in force; the ambush rose; their retreat was cut off; captives and heads were beyond counting; the rebel stockades were utterly destroyed; he advanced to lift the siege of Dayi and was granted a second-rank hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe posted elite troops in ambush along the river while leading a decoy force of weaker men; when the rebels poured out, the ambush struck and sealed their retreat, inflicting countless casualties and leveling their camps; he then relieved the siege of Dayi and was granted a second-rank hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 駱秉章督師蒞蜀，檄中和偕緒軍援綿州。

translations.literal: Luo Bingzhang arrived in Sichuan to command the army and ordered Zhonghe to join the relief forces at Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Bingzhang took command in Sichuan, he ordered Zhonghe to march with the relief column to Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 滇匪藍朝柱在諸賊中最狡悍，圍綿州日久。

translations.literal: Among the Yunnan rebels, Lan Chaozhu was the most cunning and fierce, and had long besieged Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Yunnan rebels, Lan Chaozhu was the craftiest and hardest fighter, and had kept Mianzhou under siege for a long time.

sentences.zh: 軍至，連破之，圍始解，又敗之西山觀。

translations.literal: When the army arrived, it defeated them in succession and the siege was lifted; they were defeated again at Xishan Guan.
translations.idiomatic: After the relief force arrived, it beat them repeatedly until the siege was raised, then routed them again at Xishan Pass.

sentences.zh: 朝柱竄丹棱，與李永和合攻眉州。

translations.literal: Chaozhu fled to Danling and joined Li Yonghe in a joint attack on Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozhu withdrew to Danling and united with Li Yonghe to assault Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 中和馳援，賊分路來撲，中和突陣，矛傷顋，血殷衣，不顧，奮擊破之，解眉州圍。

translations.literal: Zhonghe rushed to relieve; the rebels came at him on separate roads; Zhonghe charged the line; a spear wounded his cheek; blood soaked his robes; he paid no heed and fought on fiercely until they were broken and the siege of Meizhou was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe hurried to the rescue; the rebels struck from several directions; he broke through the formation, took a spear wound to the cheek that drenched his coat in blood, ignored it, and fought on until the enemy was shattered and Meizhou was saved.

sentences.zh: 進攻丹棱，朝柱遁走，復其城，以提督記名。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Danling, Chaozhu fled; the city was recovered; he was recorded by name for provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the attack on Danling; Chaozhu fled; the city was retaken; and he was placed on the register for provincial commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，擢雲南提督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he was promoted to provincial commander-in-chief of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign (1862), he was promoted to provincial commander-in-chief of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 李永和自眉州敗後，竄踞青神，諸軍進剿，數敗之，永和遁犍為龍場，負嵎死抗。

translations.literal: After Li Yonghe was defeated at Meizhou, he fled to seize Qing Shen; the various armies advanced to suppress him and defeated him repeatedly; Yonghe fled to Longchang in Qianwei, leaning on rugged terrain and fighting to the death.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat at Meizhou, Li Yonghe seized Qing Shen; government forces closed in, defeated him repeatedly, and drove him to Longchang in Qianwei, where he held out in rough country and resisted to the last.

sentences.zh: 中和圍之，壘石牆，編木柵，外浚深壕，密布梅花椿。

translations.literal: Zhonghe besieged him, building stone walls, weaving wooden palisades, digging deep moats outside, and densely planting caltrop stakes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe invested the position with stone walls, wooden palisades, outer trenches, and dense fields of caltrop stakes.

sentences.zh: 賊知必死，突攻蕭慶高營，中和截擊，敗退，連戰七日。

translations.literal: Knowing they were doomed, the rebels made a sortie against Xiao Qinggao's camp; Zhonghe intercepted and beat them back; fighting continued for seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no escape, the rebels stormed Xiao Qinggao's camp; Zhonghe cut them off and drove them back; the fighting lasted seven days.

sentences.zh: 賊伏不出，乃使降賊譚仁曲持書約降，期會於豬市坡，預伏兵賊巢旁。

translations.literal: The rebels lay hidden and would not come out; he then had the surrendered rebel Tan Renqu carry a letter offering surrender, fixing a meeting at Zhushipo, and stationed troops in ambush beside the rebel nest.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels refused to show themselves, he sent the defector Tan Renqu with a surrender offer and a rendezvous at Zhushipo, while hiding troops beside their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 永和與其黨卯得興數十騎來會，伏起分攻，焚其巢。

translations.literal: Yonghe came to the meeting with his partisan Mao Dexing and several dozen horsemen; the ambush rose and attacked from several sides, burning their nest.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghe appeared with Mao Dexing and a few dozen horsemen; the ambush sprang up on every side and burned out their lair.

sentences.zh: 永和、得興駭奔，追擒之，降其眾五千。

translations.literal: Yonghe and Dexing fled in panic; pursued and captured; five thousand of their followers surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghe and Dexing fled in terror, were run down and captured, and five thousand of their men surrendered.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉中和運籌決勝，生擒渠魁，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: An edict praised Zhonghe for devising the plan and winning the decisive victory and capturing the ringleader alive; he was granted the yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended Zhonghe for his strategy, decisive victory, and capture of the rebel chief alive, and awarded him the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 石達開擾蜀邊，中和偕蕭慶高、何勝必合擊於橫江，走之。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai harassed the Sichuan border; Zhonghe together with Xiao Qinggao and He Shengbi jointly attacked him at Hengjiang and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Dakai raided the Sichuan frontier, Zhonghe, Xiao Qinggao, and He Shengbi combined at Hengjiang and drove him away.

sentences.zh: 二年春，達開復分路犯蜀，自率大隊數万由米糧壩渡金沙江。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year, Dakai again divided his forces to invade Shu; he himself led a host of tens of thousands across the Jinsha River at Miliangba.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year (1863), Dakai again split his army to invade Sichuan; he personally led tens of thousands across the Jinsha at Miliangba.

sentences.zh: 中和督軍扼化林坪、瀘定橋，擊破之，賊走工卩部土司山中，達開旋就擒。

translations.literal: Zhonghe directed the army to hold Huaping and Luding Bridge, defeated them, the rebels fled into the mountains of the Gongbu native chieftain, and Dakai was soon captured.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe blocked Huaping and Luding Bridge, broke the rebel column, and chased them into the Gongbu chieftain's hills; Dakai was captured soon after.

sentences.zh: 調四川提督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to provincial commander-in-chief of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to provincial commander-in-chief of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 三年，破滇匪於敘永廳。

translations.literal: In the third year, he defeated Yunnan rebels at Xuyong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1864), he defeated Yunnan rebels in the Xuyong district.

sentences.zh: 初，李永和既誅，餘黨竄陝西，至是入甘肅，陷階州。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Li Yonghe had been executed, his remnant bands fled to Shaanxi; by this time they had entered Gansu and taken Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Yonghe's execution, his surviving followers had fled into Shaanxi; they now crossed into Gansu and seized Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，中和偕總兵周達武往剿，毀龍王廟、三官殿賊壘，逼階州城下，掘地道轟城，克之，斬賊酋蔡昌齡，盡殲其黨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Zhonghe together with Major General Zhou Dawu went to suppress them, destroyed the rebel stockades at Longwang Temple and Sanguan Hall, pressed under the walls of Jiezhou, dug a tunnel to blast the walls, captured the city, beheaded the rebel chief Cai Changling, and annihilated his entire band.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1865), Zhonghe and Major General Zhou Dawu campaigned against them, stormed the camps at Longwang Temple and Sanguan Hall, pushed to the walls of Jiezhou, mined the fortifications, took the city, executed the rebel chief Cai Changling, and wiped out his followers.

sentences.zh: 階州平，被珍賚。

translations.literal: When Jiezhou was pacified, he received imperial gifts.
translations.idiomatic: With Jiezhou pacified, he received imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 冬，剿苗匪於建武，腰中彈傷，力戰敗之。

translations.literal: In winter, he suppressed Miao bandits at Jianwu; a bullet struck him in the waist; he fought on fiercely and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he fought Miao rebels at Jianwu, took a bullet in the waist, and still pressed the battle until they were beaten.

sentences.zh: 五年，剿屏山賊，解馬邊廳圍，誅賊酋宋任傑等，餘匪悉平。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he suppressed rebels at Pingshan, lifted the siege of Mabian, executed the rebel chiefs Song Renjie and others, and the remaining bandits were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1866), he crushed the Pingshan rebels, relieved Mabian, executed the chiefs Song Renjie and others, and cleared out the rest.

sentences.zh: 十三年，調雲南提督。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was transferred to provincial commander-in-chief of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year (1874), he was transferred to provincial commander-in-chief of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，抵任。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu, he arrived to take up his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Guangxu reign (1876), he arrived to take office.

sentences.zh: 三年，平騰越夷匪。

translations.literal: In the third year, he pacified Yi bandits in Tengyue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1877), he pacified tribal rebels in Tengyue.

sentences.zh: 七年，丁母憂歸里。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, on his mother's death he returned home in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1881), he went home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒，賜卹。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he died; posthumous honors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1883), he died, and posthumous honors were granted.

sentences.zh: 何勝必，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: He Shengbi was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He Shengbi came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，勝必應募入湘軍，從蕭啟江轉戰江西、廣西，積功至副將。

translations.literal: In the Xianfeng period, Shengbi answered the call and entered the Xiang Army; he followed Xiao Qijiang fighting in Jiangxi and Guangxi and through merit reached deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianfeng era, Shengbi enlisted in the Xiang Army, campaigned with Xiao Qijiang in Jiangxi and Guangxi, and rose through merit to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 從入蜀，分統湘果右軍，破李永和於井研，又破之於資州，陣斬賊酋王二官，賜號禦勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Following the army into Shu, he took command of the right wing of the Xiang Guo Corps, defeated Li Yonghe at Jingyan, defeated him again at Zizhou, slew the rebel chief Wang Erguan in battle, and was granted the title Yuyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Sichuan with the army, commanded the right wing of the Xiang Guo Corps, beat Li Yonghe at Jingyan and again at Zizhou, killed the rebel chief Wang Erguan in the field, and received the title Yuyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 十一年，會破滇匪藍朝柱於西山觀，又敗諸青衣壩，解眉州圍，追至青神，擒斬甚眾，授甘肅肅州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he joined in defeating the Yunnan rebel Lan Chaozhu at Xishan Guan, defeated them again at Qingyi Dam, lifted the siege of Meizhou, pursued to Qing Shen, captured and slew a great many, and was appointed major general of the Suzhou Garrison in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1861), he helped rout Lan Chaozhu at Xishan Pass, beat him again at Qingyi Dam, saved Meizhou, pursued to Qing Shen, and killed or captured a great number before being appointed major general of the Suzhou garrison in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，會諸軍克青神，追賊宜賓，擒賊目周廷光。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he joined the various armies in capturing Qing Shen, pursued the rebels to Yibin, and captured the rebel leader Zhou Tingguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi (1862), he helped take Qing Shen, chased the rebels to Yibin, and captured the rebel officer Zhou Tingguang.

sentences.zh: 偕胡中和誘擒李永和於犍為龍場，二年，偕蕭慶高援漢中，戰油坊街，不利，漢中、城固相繼陷，革職留軍。

translations.literal: Together with Hu Zhonghe he lured and captured Li Yonghe at Longchang in Qianwei; in the second year, together with Xiao Qinggao he relieved Hanzhong; at the battle of Youfang Street the outcome was unfavorable; Hanzhong and Chenggu fell in succession; he was stripped of rank but kept with the army.
translations.idiomatic: With Hu Zhonghe he trapped and captured Li Yonghe at Longchang in Qianwei; in the second year (1863) he marched with Xiao Qinggao to Hanzhong, was beaten at Youfang Street, and after Hanzhong and Chenggu fell in turn was dismissed from office but kept on campaign.

sentences.zh: 三年，會攻法慈院賊壘，再敗之牟家壩，乘勝薄漢中城下，捻渠陳得才遁走，克漢中，復原官。

translations.literal: In the third year, he joined the attack on the rebel stockade at Faci Yuan, defeated them again at Moujiaba, rode the victory to press under the walls of Hanzhong; the Nian chief Chen Deicai fled; Hanzhong was captured and his former rank restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1864), he helped storm the Faci Yuan camp, routed the enemy again at Moujiaba, pressed to the walls of Hanzhong, drove off the Nian leader Chen Deicai, retook the city, and had his rank restored.

sentences.zh: 又破陳得才於上元觀，克城固，進規階州。

translations.literal: He again defeated Chen Deicai at Shangyuan Guan, captured Chenggu, and advanced to invest Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Chen Deicai again at Shangyuan Pass, retook Chenggu, and moved to besiege Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒於軍，賜卹，諡威愨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he died in the army; posthumous honors were granted; his posthumous title was Weike.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1865), he died on campaign; posthumous honors were granted, and he was given the posthumous title Weike.

sentences.zh: 蕭慶高，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Xiao Qinggao was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Qinggao came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 隸楚軍，積功至副將。

translations.literal: He belonged to the Chu Army and through merit reached deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Chu Army and rose through merit to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 蕭啟江援蜀，調從軍，以井研之捷，賜號果勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When Xiao Qijiang relieved Shu, he was transferred to follow the army; for the victory at Jingyan he was granted the title Guoyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Qijiang marched into Sichuan, he was assigned to the campaign; for the victory at Jingyan he received the title Guoyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 破李永和於資州，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: He defeated Li Yonghe at Zizhou and was recorded by name for major general.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Li Yonghe at Zizhou and was placed on the register for major general.

sentences.zh: 會剿藍朝柱，解綿州圍。

translations.literal: He joined the campaign against Lan Chaozhu and lifted the siege of Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaign against Lan Chaozhu and raised the siege of Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，偕何勝必援漢中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi, he together with He Shengbi relieved Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongzhi (1863), he marched with He Shengbi to relieve Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 油坊街之戰，勝必先敗，慶高赴援不及，同革職留軍。

translations.literal: At the battle of Youfang Street, Shengbi was defeated first; Qinggao could not arrive in time to relieve him; both were stripped of rank but kept with the army.
translations.idiomatic: At Youfang Street, Shengbi was beaten first and Qinggao could not reach him in time; both men lost their ranks but remained on campaign.

sentences.zh: 三年，克漢中，同复官。

translations.literal: In the third year, Hanzhong was captured and both had their ranks restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1864), Hanzhong was retaken and both had their ranks restored.

sentences.zh: 追賊至城固，梯城而入，賊潰走。

translations.literal: Pursuing the rebels to Chenggu, they scaled the walls with ladders; the rebels broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing the enemy to Chenggu, they went over the walls on ladders and sent the rebels fleeing.

sentences.zh: 四年，進攻洋縣，遣死士入城為內應，克之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, advancing to attack Yang County, he sent daredevils into the city as inside agents and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1865), besieging Yang County, he slipped daredevils inside as agents and took the city.

sentences.zh: 賊酋曹燦章走踞八里坪，夾攻破之，燦章就擒，授漢中鎮總兵。

translations.literal: The rebel chief Cao Canzhang fled to hold Bali Ping; attacked and defeated from both sides, Canzhang was captured and he was appointed major general of the Hanzhong Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chief Cao Canzhang fell back to Bali Ping; Qinggao crushed him in a pincer attack, took Canzhang alive, and was appointed major general of the Hanzhong garrison.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，諡武毅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he died; his posthumous title was Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1866), he died and was given the posthumous title Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 楊復東，湖南瀏陽人。

translations.literal: Yang Fudong was a native of Liuyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fudong came from Liuyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，從胡中和援蜀。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng, he followed Hu Zhonghe to relieve Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xianfeng (1860), he followed Hu Zhonghe into Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 十一年，戰富順牛腹渡，解大邑圍，擢守備。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he fought at Niufudu in Fushun, lifted the siege of Dayi, and was promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1861), he fought at Niufudu in Fushun, helped relieve Dayi, and was promoted to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 敗藍朝柱於綿州，擢都司。

translations.literal: He defeated Lan Chaozhu at Mianzhou and was promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Lan Chaozhu at Mianzhou and was promoted to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 又破朝柱於崇慶，毀石羊場，焚賊巢，擢游擊。

translations.literal: He again defeated Chaozhu at Chongqing, destroyed Shiyangchang, burned the rebel nest, and was promoted to brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: He beat Chaozhu again at Chongqing, destroyed Shiyangchang, burned the rebel stronghold, and was promoted to brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，复丹棱，擢參將。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he recovered Danling and was promoted to regimental commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi (1862), he retook Danling and was promoted to regimental commander.

sentences.zh: 克青神，平鐵山賊壘，擒李永和。

translations.literal: He captured Qing Shen, leveled the rebel stockade at Tieshan, and captured Li Yonghe.
translations.idiomatic: He took Qing Shen, stormed the Tieshan rebel camp, and helped capture Li Yonghe.

sentences.zh: 擢副將。

translations.literal: He was promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 五年，總督駱秉章疏陳復東歷年防剿滇、黔諸賊功多，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Governor-General Luo Bingzhang memorialized that Fudong over the years had achieved much in defending against and suppressing Yunnan and Guizhou rebels; he was recorded by name for major general.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1866), Governor-General Luo Bingzhang reported Fudong's long record against Yunnan and Guizhou rebels and had him placed on the register for major general.

sentences.zh: 七年，授四川川北鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was appointed major general of the Chuanbei Garrison in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1868), he was appointed major general of the Chuanbei garrison in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，調雲南開化鎮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu, he was transferred to the Kaifa Garrison in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Guangxu reign (1876), he was transferred to the Kaifa garrison in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1880), he died.

sentences.zh: 周達武，字夢熊，湖南寧鄉人。

translations.literal: Zhou Dawu, style name Mengxiong, was a native of Ningxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dawu, whose courtesy name was Mengxiong, came from Ningxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，應募入李續賓營，從克岳州、武昌，累功擢守備。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng, he answered the call and entered Li Xubin's camp; he followed in capturing Yuezhou and Wuchang and through accumulated merit was promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianfeng (1854), he enlisted in Li Xubin's command, helped take Yuezhou and Wuchang, and rose through merit to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 戰湖口，晉都司。

translations.literal: Fighting at Hukou, he was promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: After fighting at Hukou, he was promoted to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 達武每戰陷陣，手大旗盪決，續賓異之，使領百人曰信字營，常為軍鋒。

translations.literal: Dawu in every battle charged the line, wielding a great banner to break through; Xubin regarded him as extraordinary and had him lead a hundred men called the Xinzi Battalion, and he was often the army's spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: In every fight Dawu led the charge, brandishing his standard to break the enemy line; Xubin singled him out to command a hundred-man unit called the Xinzi Battalion, and he often served as the army's spearhead.

sentences.zh: 八年，克黃安，擢游擊，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Huang'an was captured; he was promoted to brigade commander and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1858), he helped take Huang'an, was promoted to brigade commander, and received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 從續賓攻舒城，達武率死士先登，左耳受槍傷，克城後，留守。

translations.literal: Following Xubin in the attack on Shucheng, Dawu led daredevils to scale the walls first; his left ear was struck by a musket ball; after the city was taken he remained to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Shucheng with Xubin, Dawu led the scaling party; a musket ball tore his left ear; after the city fell he was left to hold it.

sentences.zh: 俄續賓覆軍三河，舒城守軍亦潰，達武以創重回湖南。

translations.literal: Soon Xubin's army was destroyed at Sanhe; the Shucheng garrison also collapsed; Dawu returned to Hunan with his wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xubin's force was wiped out at Sanhe, the Shucheng garrison collapsed as well, and Dawu went home to Hunan to recover from his wounds.

sentences.zh: 九年，石達開圍寶慶，巡撫駱秉章令達武募五百人號曰章武軍，從知府劉岳昭援寶慶，守東關，屢拒戰破賊。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Shi Dakai besieged Baqing; Governor Luo Bingzhang ordered Dawu to recruit five hundred men called the Zhangwu Army; following Prefect Liu Yuezhao to relieve Baqing, he guarded the east gate and repeatedly repelled the rebels in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1859), when Shi Dakai besieged Baqing, Governor Luo Bingzhang had Dawu raise five hundred men as the Zhangwu Army; marching with Prefect Liu Yuezhao to the relief, he held the east gate and repeatedly beat back rebel assaults.

sentences.zh: 圍解，擢參將。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted, he was promoted to regimental commander.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege was raised, he was promoted to regimental commander.

sentences.zh: 十年，援廣西，克富川平古城、連塘賊壘，复賀縣，擢副將，加總兵銜。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he relieved Guangxi, captured the rebel stockades at Pinggucheng and Liantang in Fuchuan, recovered Hexian, was promoted to deputy commander, and given major-general rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1860), he campaigned in Guangxi, took the rebel camps at Pinggucheng and Liantang in Fuchuan, retook Hexian, was promoted to deputy commander, and received major-general rank.

sentences.zh: 石達開分黨犯永明、柘牌，連戰破之，擢總兵。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai sent partisans to attack Yongming and Zhepai; Dawu defeated them in successive battles and was promoted to major general.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Dakai detached forces against Yongming and Zhepai, Dawu defeated them in a series of engagements and was promoted to major general.

sentences.zh: 十一年，會諸軍克會同，賊走湖北，陷來鳳。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he joined the various armies in capturing Huitong; the rebels fled to Hubei and took Laifeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1861), he helped take Huitong; the rebels fled into Hubei and seized Laifeng.

sentences.zh: 同治元年春，從劉岳昭攻克之，予二品封典。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Tongzhi, following Liu Yuezhao he captured it and was granted a second-rank hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first Tongzhi year (1862), he followed Liu Yuezhao in retaking Laifeng and was granted a second-rank hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 駱秉章督師四川，調達武從剿。

translations.literal: Luo Bingzhang commanded the army in Sichuan and transferred Dawu to follow the suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Bingzhang took command in Sichuan, Dawu was ordered into the pacification campaign.

sentences.zh: 抵涪州，會賊酋周紹勇由大寧竄陝西，達武扼之窄子口，地當兩山間，令部將李輝武逾險而入，賊潰走，追至大竹安吉場，擒紹勇及其黨吳崇禮等，檻送成都斬之，賜號質勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Reaching Fuzhou, he encountered the rebel chief Zhou Shaoyong fleeing from Daning into Shaanxi; Dawu blocked him at Zhaizikou, a place between two mountains; he ordered his subordinate Li Huiwu to cross the dangerous terrain and enter; the rebels broke and fled; pursued to Anji Chang in Dazhu, Shaoyong and his partisan Wu Chongli and others were captured, sent in a caged cart to Chengdu and executed; he was granted the title Zhiyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: At Fuzhou he intercepted the rebel chief Zhou Shaoyong as he fled from Daning toward Shaanxi, blocked him at Zhaizikou between two mountain ranges, and sent Li Huiwu over the heights to strike; the rebels scattered; he ran them down to Anji Field in Dazhu, captured Shaoyong and Wu Chongli, sent them in a cage to Chengdu for execution, and received the title Zhiyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 又破郭刀刀於儀隴大​​儀寨，陣斬其弟佔彪及悍黨馬玉音，追奔至巴州鼎山鋪，擒刀刀，餘黨皆降。

translations.literal: He again defeated Guo Daodao at Dayizhai in Yilong, slew in battle his younger brother Zhanbiao and the fierce partisan Ma Yuyin, pursued the flight to Dingshanpu in Bazhou, captured Daodao, and the remaining partisans all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He next defeated Guo Daodao at Dayizhai in Yilong, killed his brother Zhanbiao and the hardened fighter Ma Yuyin in the field, chased the survivors to Dingshan Station in Bazhou, captured Daodao, and accepted the surrender of the rest.

sentences.zh: 紹勇與刀刀並為蜀中劇賊，至是悉平，授四川建昌鎮總兵，加提督銜。

translations.literal: Shaoyong and Daodao were together the fiercest rebels in Shu; by this time both were pacified; he was appointed major general of the Jianchang Garrison in Sichuan with provincial commander-in-chief rank added.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyong and Daodao had been the worst rebels in Sichuan; with both gone he was appointed major general of the Jianchang garrison and given provincial commander-in-chief rank.

sentences.zh: 二年，護理提督。

translations.literal: In the second year, he acted as provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1863), he served as acting provincial commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 粵匪陳得才圍漢中，眾號十萬，石達開亦由高縣走寧遠，全蜀大震。

translations.literal: The Cantonese rebel Chen Deicai besieged Hanzhong; his force was said to number one hundred thousand; Shi Dakai also marched from Gaoxian toward Ningyuan; all of Shu was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Deicai of the Taiping forces besieged Hanzhong with a host said to number one hundred thousand, while Shi Dakai marched from Gaoxian toward Ningyuan; the whole of Sichuan was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 達武增募軍四千人，往來游擊。

translations.literal: Dawu enlarged his army by four thousand men and ranged back and forth in mobile attacks.
translations.idiomatic: Dawu raised another four thousand troops and ranged the province in mobile strikes.

sentences.zh: 三年，得才之黨梁福成合川匪蔡昌齡由漢中竄甘肅階州，達武議以剿為防，率師越境，攻克江東水、嚴家灣賊壘。

translations.literal: In the third year, Deicai's partisan Liang Fucheng together with the Sichuan rebel Cai Changling fled from Hanzhong into Jiezhou in Gansu; Dawu argued that offense was the best defense, led his army across the border, and captured the rebel stockades at Jiangdongshui and Yanjiawan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1864), Liang Fucheng, a lieutenant of Deicai, joined the Sichuan rebel Cai Changling in a breakout from Hanzhong into Jiezhou, Gansu; Dawu held that the best defense was attack, crossed the border, and stormed the camps at Jiangdongshui and Yanjiawan.

sentences.zh: 進攻階州，自將台山穴地達城根，地雷發，城崩，選鋒四百人先入，大軍繼之，遂克階州，斬福成、昌齡。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Jiezhou, he himself tunneled from Jiangtai Hill to reach the base of the wall; the land mine exploded and the wall collapsed; four hundred picked troops entered first and the main army followed; Jiezhou was thus captured and Fucheng and Changling were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Besieging Jiezhou, he drove a mine from Jiangtai Hill to the foot of the wall; when it blew, the ramparts fell; four hundred picked men rushed in first and the main force followed; the city was taken and Fucheng and Changling were executed.

sentences.zh: 以提督記名，並頒珍賚。

translations.literal: He was recorded by name for provincial commander-in-chief and also received imperial gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He was placed on the register for provincial commander-in-chief and received imperial gifts as well.

sentences.zh: 尋平松潘叛番，授貴州提督，仍留防重慶，備滇邊。

translations.literal: Soon after he pacified rebellious Tibetans in Songpan, was appointed provincial commander-in-chief of Guizhou, yet remained to defend Chongqing and guard the Yunnan frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He soon pacified the Tibetan revolt in Songpan, was appointed provincial commander-in-chief of Guizhou, but stayed on to hold Chongqing and watch the Yunnan border.

sentences.zh: 五年，剿平馬邊廳教匪，斬匪首宋仕傑、熊文才。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he suppressed the sect rebels of Mabian, beheading the rebel leaders Song Shijie and Xiong Wencai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1866), he put down the religious rebels in Mabian and executed the chiefs Song Shijie and Xiong Wencai.

sentences.zh: 六年，捻匪竄陝西，左宗棠諮調會剿，令部將李輝武率三千赴陝。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Nian rebels fled into Shaanxi; Zuo Zongtang consulted and transferred him to join the campaign; he ordered his subordinate Li Huiwu to lead three thousand into Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1867), when Nian rebels crossed into Shaanxi, Zuo Zongtang called Dawu to the joint campaign and sent Li Huiwu ahead with three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 七年，破越巂倮夷於普雄，進克西昌交腳夷巢，斬級數千，諸夷悉降，賜黃馬褂，晉號博奇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he defeated the Lolo tribes of Yuexi at Puxiong, advanced to capture the Jiaojiao Yi nest at Xichang, beheaded several thousand, and all the tribes surrendered; he was granted the yellow riding jacket and his title was advanced to Boqi Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1868), he defeated the Yi of Yuexi at Puxiong, stormed the Jiaojiao Yi stronghold at Xichang, took several thousand heads, and brought every tribe to submission; he received the yellow riding jacket and an advancement of his title to Boqi Batulu.

sentences.zh: 九年，詔赴貴州提督任，率所部六千人行，沿途平苗砦。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was ordered to proceed to his post as provincial commander-in-chief of Guizhou, led his own division of six thousand men on the march, and along the way pacified Miao stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1870), an imperial order sent him to take up the Guizhou command; he marched with six thousand men of his division and cleared Miao stockades all along the route.

sentences.zh: 先是貴州剿寇仰客軍，出省城百里即莫能製馭。

translations.literal: Previously Guizhou's bandit suppression had relied on guest armies; a hundred li beyond the provincial capital they could no longer control them.
translations.idiomatic: Until then Guizhou had depended on outside armies for pacification; beyond a hundred li from the capital those troops could no longer be kept in hand.

sentences.zh: 達武與巡撫議增募至三萬人，分任戰守，由龍里進凱渡，截上下游賊為二，复都勻，分軍破賊永寧、威寧。

translations.literal: Dawu and the governor discussed increasing recruitment to thirty thousand men, divided duties between campaigning and garrison, advanced from Longli to Kaidu, cut the rebels of the upper and lower reaches into two, recovered Duyun, and divided the army to defeat rebels at Yongning and Weining.
translations.idiomatic: Dawu and the governor agreed to raise strength to thirty thousand, split forces between field and garrison duty, advanced from Longli toward Kaidu, severed the rebel positions above and below the line, retook Duyun, and detached columns to break the enemy at Yongning and Weining.

sentences.zh: 十年，遣鍾開蘭攻克麻哈州之高水塘等地數十砦；

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he sent Zhong Kailan to capture dozens of stockades such as Gaoshuitang in Mahazhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1871) he sent Zhong Kailan to storm dozens of stockades, including Gaoshuitang in Mahazhou;

sentences.zh: 遣何世華破粵賊李文彩、苗酋李高腳於都勻、獨山，收復八寨、三腳諸城，並克鎮寧、歸化及吳秀河、斑竹園諸苗砦，復清平、黃平二城。

translations.literal: He sent He Shihua to defeat the Cantonese rebel Li Wencai and the Miao chief Li Gaojiao at Duyun and Dushan, recovered the cities of Bazhai, Sanjiao, and others, and also captured Zhenning, Guihua, and the Miao stockades at Wuxiuhe and Banzhuyuan, recovering the two cities of Qingping and Huangping.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched He Shihua to rout the Cantonese rebel Li Wencai and the Miao chief Li Gaojiao at Duyun and Dushan, retook Bazhai, Sanjiao, and neighboring towns, seized Zhenning, Guihua, and the Miao forts at Wuxiuhe and Banzhuyuan, and restored Qingping and Huangping.

sentences.zh: 始與楚軍席寶田合。

translations.literal: He first joined forces with Xi Baotian of the Chu army.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the Hunan forces under Xi Baotian.

sentences.zh: 十一年，會席軍敗苗酋張臭迷之黨於茶牛坡，斬馘甚眾，降者數万。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he joined Xi's army to defeat the party of the Miao chief Zhang Choumi at Chaniu Slope; heads taken and slain were very numerous, and those who surrendered numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1872) he and Xi's troops routed the followers of the Miao chief Zhang Choumi at Chaniu Slope, took a great toll in heads, and accepted the surrender of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 追至冷水溝，生擒賊酋，餘黨李高腳、李文彩竄荊蓬坎，分三路追擊，盡殄之。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Lengshuigou, he captured the rebel chief alive; the remainder, Li Gaojiao and Li Wencai, fled to Jingpengkan; he pursued on three routes and annihilated them all.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit reached Lengshuigou, where the rebel chief was taken alive; Li Gaojiao and Li Wencai fled to Jingpengkan, and a three-pronged pursuit wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 旋破群苗於清平香爐山，寶田擒張臭迷。

translations.literal: Soon after he defeated the Miao masses at Xianglu Hill in Qingping; Baotian captured Zhang Choumi.
translations.idiomatic: He next broke the Miao hosts at Xianglu Hill near Qingping, and Baotian captured Zhang Choumi.

sentences.zh: 苗疆平，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: The Miao frontier was pacified, and he was granted a hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: With the Miao frontier pacified, he received a hereditary rank as Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，乞病歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu, he requested leave on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu (1875), he asked to retire on account of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 三年，授甘肅提督。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was appointed provincial commander-in-chief of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1877), he was appointed provincial commander-in-chief of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 十年，肅州妖民王林倡亂高台，討平之，斬王林。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the sorcerous commoner Wang Lin of Suzhou raised rebellion at Gaotai; he suppressed it and beheaded Wang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1884), the sorcerer Wang Lin of Suzhou stirred up revolt at Gaotai; Dawu put it down and executed Wang Lin.

sentences.zh: 十九年，萬壽慶典，加尚書銜。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, at the Wan Shou celebration, he was given the added rank of Minister.
translations.idiomatic: At the nineteenth-year longevity celebration (1893), he received the added rank of Minister.

sentences.zh: 二十年，卒官，賜卹，建專祠。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he died in office; condolence gifts were granted and a dedicated shrine was built.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year (1894), he died in office; the court granted mourning favors and ordered a private shrine built in his honor.

sentences.zh: 弟康祿，從達武勦賊廣西、湖南，歷保知縣。

translations.literal: His younger brother Kang Lu followed Dawu in suppressing rebels in Guangxi and Hunan and was repeatedly promoted to the rank of magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Kang Lu campaigned with Dawu in Guangxi and Hunan and rose through repeated recommendations to magistrate.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從赴蜀，破周紹勇，擢知州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he followed him to Shu, defeated Zhou Shaoyong, and was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Tongzhi year (1862), he followed Dawu into Sichuan, helped defeat Zhou Shaoyong, and was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 四年，從克階州，擢知府。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he followed in the capture of Jiezhou and was promoted to prefectural magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1865), he took part in the capture of Jiezhou and was raised to prefectural magistrate.

sentences.zh: 從至貴州，總理營務。

translations.literal: He followed him to Guizhou and supervised camp affairs in general.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Dawu to Guizhou and took charge of camp administration.

sentences.zh: 十一年，下游肅清，擢道員。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, the lower reaches were cleared; he was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1872), with the lower river country pacified, he was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 駐軍普安新城，招撫流亡。

translations.literal: He garrisoned the army at Pu'an New City and recruited and pacified the displaced.
translations.idiomatic: He stationed troops at Pu'an New City and brought refugees back under government protection.

sentences.zh: 十二年，會匪煽亂，康祿督親軍百人往討，眾寡不敵，死之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Society rebels incited disorder; Kang Lu led a hundred men of his personal guard to attack; outnumbered, he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (1873), secret-society rebels stirred up trouble; Kang Lu led a hundred of his household troops against them, was overwhelmed, and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈內閣學士，予騎都尉世職，諡壯節。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Inner Court Academician, given a hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant, and given the posthumous name Zhuangjie.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him an Inner Court Academician, granted a hereditary Cavalry Commandant rank, and gave him the posthumous name Zhuangjie (Stalwart Integrity).

sentences.zh: 李輝武，湖南衡山人。

translations.literal: Li Huiwu was a native of Hengshan in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huiwu came from Hengshan in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 周達武部將。

translations.literal: A subordinate officer of Zhou Dawu.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a brigade commander under Zhou Dawu.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，從剿粵匪，洊擢游擊。

translations.literal: During the Xianfeng reign he followed in suppressing the Cantonese rebels and was repeatedly promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianfeng era he campaigned against the Taiping forces in Guangdong and rose by repeated merit to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從入四川，剿涪川鶴遊坪踞賊，擒賊酋周紹勇、郭刀刀。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he followed into Sichuan, suppressed the rebels holding Heyouping in Fuchuan, and captured the rebel chiefs Zhou Shaoyong and Guo Daodao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1861), he entered Sichuan, cleared the rebels entrenched at Heyouping in Fuchuan, and captured the chiefs Zhou Shaoyong and Guo Daodao.

sentences.zh: 輝武功為多，擢副將，賜號武勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Huiwu's merit was the greater part; he was promoted to deputy commander and granted the title Wuyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Huiwu's deeds ranked foremost; he was made deputy commander and given the title Wuyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，從援階州，輝武由伍家坪進軍，扼州城外北山條竹埡。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi, he followed in relieving Jiezhou; Huiwu advanced from Wujiaping and held Tiaozhuya on the northern hill outside the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Tongzhi year (1864), marching to relieve Jiezhou, Huiwu advanced from Wujiaping and seized Tiaozhuya on the north hill outside the city walls.
